messages:
acme-qa: Hey team, hitting an issue with streaming responses — while we stream a ~4k token generation we get a disconnect mid-stream and a 429 in the client logs. Billing shows a token delta that doesn't match what we received. Need urgent help; this is blocking our demo tomorrow.

acme-qa: Repro steps: we open an SSE to /v1/streams with Authorization header and stream=true. Shortly after ~1800 tokens emitted the connection closed and our client got an HTTP/1.1 200 (SSE) then an immediate 429 body in a JSON chunk. We don't close the connection. curl shows: 

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-lg","prompt":"<huge prompt>","max_tokens":4096,"stream":true}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
```

acme-qa: Server-side they see partial text saved to DB but billing shows we were charged for entire 4k tokens, yet we only received ~1800. Also the client side token counters show mismatch (client counted 1800).

maria: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the raw SSE frames you received (a few last ones) and any X-RateLimit headers from the 429 chunk? Also which SDK / proxy (nginx, Cloudflare) is in front of you?

acme-qa: Logs: 

```
data: {"id":"evt_abc","delta":"...","role":"assistant"}

data: {"id":"evt_abc","delta":"..."}

# then connection socket close, our client emitted:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream

# then an inline json frame arrived from the stream body:
{"error": {"type":"rate_limit","message":"quota exceeded mid-stream","code":429}, "headers": {"X-RateLimit-Limit":"100000","X-RateLimit-Remaining":"0"}}
```

acme-qa: We're running behind a customer-managed proxy (nginx) and also a small concurrency limiter in our app. No Cloudflare. SDK is our own TS client using EventSource polyfill in Node.

alex: Thanks — couple possibilities: 1) Redwood rate limiter detected quota exhaustion and injected an error event into the open SSE (we do that currently), which explains the 429 JSON frame mid-stream. 2) Token accounting bug where billing increments were recorded for the reservation at stream start, but the client saw fewer bytes because the server truncated before finalization. We'll investigate. Do you have a request id or X-Request-Id from the initial response?

acme-qa: We log `x-request-id: req_0a7f9` from the TLS connection. Also saw `x-redwood-stream-id: s_91b2` in the initial headers.

chris: I'm going to correlate those IDs in logs. Quick troubleshooting for customer: please capture the initial response headers (we need Server-SSE headers), and confirm whether you are re-using the same Authorization token for any reconnects. If the client reconnects without a fresh auth token, the server may reject subsequent frames if token was revoked/limit updated.

acme-qa: We do NOT reconnect automatically — single connection. It never attempts to re-open. The 429 appears as a final JSON data frame before socket close.

maria: On our side I see a pattern: the rate limiter is conservative — when account usage crosses a usage threshold concurrent streams that are active can receive a termination error event. We intended to emit a final error frame and close, but there was a bug where we didn't decrement the provisional token reservation until the stream closed, causing billing to still charge for reserved tokens. That can lead to billed > delivered. We're triaging.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2024-0420 — streaming mid-stream 429 + token accounting mismatch. Assigned: chris. Severity: P2.

chris: Reproduction plan I'm running: spawn 3 parallel streaming requests with long max_tokens and artificially lower quota for that account. I'll simulate with our internal bench and reproduce mid-stream injection of 429. If reproduced, root cause likely race between quota enforcement path and stream finalization path that writes final token usage.

acme-qa: Appreciate that. Any short-term client-side mitigations we should apply before your fix?

maria: Yes — two practical mitigations: 1) Retry logic: treat a 429 SSE event as retriable for idempotent prompts by re-issuing a fresh request and seeking to reconstruct the missing suffix (best for stateless prompts). For stateful chats, you should checkpoint partial output and re-run remainder. 2) Add early token reservation: call a lightweight preflight endpoint that reserves expected tokens (we can do a small PR to expose a reserve API) or reduce max_tokens. Also set a small keepalive ping to detect abrupt closures faster.

alex: Also ensure on reconnect you re-send Authorization and use a unique X-Client-Request-Id. Right now we don't support resume of half-completed generations; reconnect always starts a new generation. So instruct clients to be ready to synthesize from the last valid token boundary.

acme-qa: For billing — will you refund the excess charged tokens if it's confirmed as server bug? We can't justify paying for tokens we didn't receive.

maria: Yes — if we confirm via server logs that the account was charged for tokens that were not emitted because of our bug, we will issue a credit/refund. We'll need the request/stream ids and approximate time window (you gave both). Chis, can you confirm what we need to validate and the expected ETA?

chris: Will validate today. I'll check internal usage records and the stream lifecycle logs for req_0a7f9 / s_91b2. If it matches the race, we'll schedule a refund and postmortem. ETA EOD PST.

acme-qa: Thanks — small ask: can you provide a snippet showing what a client should retry on SSE 429? Here's what we tried but it fails when server closes socket: 

```
es.on('message', (evt) => {
  let json = JSON.parse(evt.data)
  if (json.error && json.error.code === 429) {
    // we tried to reopen here
    reopenStream(); // this gets 401 if token expired sometimes
  }
})
```

maria: Suggestion: treat 429 as "retryable but reauthenticate and start fresh". Example flow: 

```
// 1) On 429 SSE frame: close EventSource
// 2) Fetch fresh token if needed
// 3) Re-open stream with the same prompt, but with a client-side checkpoint of received tokens
// 4) If server supports offsets in prompt you can request only missing suffix, otherwise re-run prompt but mark dedup at your app level
```

maria: Also ensure your nginx proxy doesn't buffer or mutate the SSE stream — set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection "";` for chunked SSE. Otherwise you can lose mid-stream frames.

acme-qa: We do have`proxy_buffering on;` — switching that off might reduce the chance of seeing garbled frames. We'll change and test.

chris: Internal note: short-term patch: we will change rate limiter to emit a terminating SSE error but also immediately flush and write final token accounting before closing. Longer-term: redesign to reserve tokens up-front or provide a reserving endpoint. I'll update INC-2024-0420 after validate.

acme-qa: Changing nginx made the error less frequent during smoke tests. Thanks. Hoping for the refund and a permanent fix.

maria: Confirmed we've located the trace for req_0a7f9 and s_91b2. We saw the rate-limit enforcement fire concurrently with the finalization path; tokens were billed at reservation time, but when we aborted mid-stream we didn't correct the ledger. We'll process a credit for the difference. I'll DM billing for credit and notify you when posted.

ops-bot: INC-2024-0420 status updated: triage done -> fix in progress.

chris: Small follow-up: can you send the raw request payload (trim sensitive data) or attach the prompt fingerprint? That will help us confirm exact token usage boundaries.

acme-qa: Shared prompt fingerprint in a DM. Thanks all, this unblocked our demo for now. :thumbsup:
